description: Each media type's byte rate is its tracks' total Bytes divided by their total Milliseconds.

b.request: For each media type, compute the average UnitPrice across all its tracks and its byte rate as SUM(Bytes) divided by SUM(Milliseconds). Keep the media types whose byte rate is above the simple (unweighted) average of byte rates across all media types. Return one row with the average of the kept types' average unit prices, the average of their byte rates, and the average of (byte rate minus the cross-media-type average byte rate) across the kept types, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, SUM(Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(Milliseconds) AS byte_rate FROM Track GROUP BY MediaTypeId), o AS (SELECT AVG(byte_rate) AS avg_br FROM m) SELECT AVG(m.avg_price) AS avg_unit_price, AVG(m.byte_rate) AS avg_byte_rate, AVG(m.byte_rate - o.avg_br) AS avg_diff FROM m CROSS JOIN o WHERE m.byte_rate > o.avg_br

a.request: For each media type (`Track.MediaTypeId`), across all tracks, work out the average track `UnitPrice` and the total `Bytes` of its tracks divided by their total `Milliseconds`. Take the simple average of that byte rate across the media types, and keep only the media types whose rate is above it. Return one row with: the average of their average unit prices, the average of their byte rates, and the average amount by which their rate exceeds the cross-media-type average (rate minus that average). Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, CAST(SUM(Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track GROUP BY MediaTypeId), g AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM m) SELECT AVG(m.avg_price) AS avg_unit_price, AVG(m.rate) AS avg_byte_rate, AVG(m.rate - g.avg_rate) AS avg_excess FROM m, g WHERE m.rate > g.avg_rate

c.request: For each media type, looking at all tracks, work out the average track unit price and its bytes per millisecond. Keep the media types whose bytes per millisecond is above the simple average across media types. Give one row with: the average of their average unit prices, the average of their bytes per millisecond, and on average how far their rate is above that cross-media-type average (rate minus average). No rounding. Each media type's byte rate is its tracks' total Bytes divided by their total Milliseconds.
c.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, CAST(SUM(Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track GROUP BY MediaTypeId), a AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM m) SELECT AVG(m.avg_price) AS avg_unit_price, AVG(m.rate) AS avg_bytes_per_ms, AVG(m.rate - a.avg_rate) AS avg_rate_above_average FROM m, a WHERE m.rate > a.avg_rate

d.request: For each media type, using all of its tracks, compute the average track unit price and the byte rate, where the byte rate is the total Bytes divided by the total Milliseconds across that media type's tracks. Keep only the media types whose byte rate is above the simple (unweighted) average of the byte rates across all media types. Return one row with three values: the average of the kept media types' average unit prices, the average of their byte rates, and the average amount by which their byte rates exceed the cross-media-type average byte rate (rate minus average). Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, CAST(SUM(Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS br FROM Track GROUP BY MediaTypeId), o AS (SELECT AVG(br) AS avg_br FROM m) SELECT AVG(m.avg_price) AS avg_unit_price, AVG(m.br) AS avg_byte_rate, AVG(m.br - o.avg_br) AS avg_excess FROM m, o WHERE m.br > o.avg_br
